sd.step.clear_outside.sourceText:
Limits: outside the grille only. No reaching in. No touching the coil or fins at all, by hand or with tools. No leaf-picking off the unit.
1. pn-v1 §8: “Do only the step shown. If anything looks different or you see a hazard sign, stop. You can always call a licensed HVAC professional.” `REUSED pn-v1 §8`
2. pn-v1 §4: “Don’t change these. They protect your equipment and your safety, and they’re for professionals only: any side, top, or front panel or cover; the electrical or control box; the disconnect box and its handle or fuses; buttons, switches, or displays on the board inside the unit; the fan blade and fan motor; refrigerant valves, caps, and pipes; the pipe cover and insulation; the stand, wall bracket, and their bolts; any heater, sensor, or wire on the unit; service menus and anything that clears or deletes stored codes or error history. If a step would take you to one of these, stop. If a screen asks you to enter a password or access code, stop. That’s for installers. Writing down an error code that’s already showing is fine.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.044`
3. What this does / Caution: “What this does: Keeps stored items, covers, and plants away from the outside of the unit so it can breathe. Caution: The fins bend easily, and the fan can start on its own at any time.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.101`
4. Source caption: `From Daikin 3P515859-5S (blocked outdoor coil listed among high-pressure fault causes) and LG’s error-code guide (clear obstacles around the outdoor unit), checked October 11, 2026.`
5. Steps: “1. Write down how the thermostat is set, then turn the system Off at the thermostat. This doesn’t cut power to the unit, so stay outside the grilles. 2. Move planters, toys, covers, and stored items away from the unit. 3. Trim plants back by hand or with hand pruners, keeping the pruners and clippings away from the unit. 4. Pick up loose leaves and clippings from the ground around the unit. Don’t touch the coil or fins at all, by hand or with any tool. Don’t reach through the grille, use a pressure washer, or spray water near the electrical side. Leave anything on the fins, stuck in them, or behind the grille for a professional. 5. Put the thermostat back the way you wrote it down.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.102`
6. Watch: “After you set the thermostat back, watch from a few steps back for about 10 minutes.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.108`
7. Stop: “Stop and put the thermostat back the way you wrote it down if anything near the electrical box is wet or icy, if you’d have to reach inside the grille, or if the fan starts while you’re close. If that doesn’t fix it, call a licensed HVAC professional.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.103`
8. Undo: pn-v1 §3 undo line (REUSED; this page only)

sd.step.clear_snow.sourceText:
Limits: around and in front of the unit only. Never clear snow off the coil face. No touching the coil or fins. No ice removal. No ladder or snowbank.
1. pn-v1 §8: “Do only the step shown. If anything looks different or you see a hazard sign, stop. You can always call a licensed HVAC professional.” `REUSED pn-v1 §8`
2. pn-v1 §4: “Don’t change these. They protect your equipment and your safety, and they’re for professionals only: any side, top, or front panel or cover; the electrical or control box; the disconnect box and its handle or fuses; buttons, switches, or displays on the board inside the unit; the fan blade and fan motor; refrigerant valves, caps, and pipes; the pipe cover and insulation; the stand, wall bracket, and their bolts; any heater, sensor, or wire on the unit; service menus and anything that clears or deletes stored codes or error history. If a step would take you to one of these, stop. If a screen asks you to enter a password or access code, stop. That’s for installers. Writing down an error code that’s already showing is fine.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.044`
3. Cold-weather line (D-024 R7, no temperature cutoff): “Turn the system Off at the thermostat while you clear around the unit, and turn it back to Heat as soon as you’re done. If anyone at home is an infant, elderly, or medically fragile, keep it brief or leave it to a professional.” `REUSED D-024 R7`
4. What this does / Caution: “What this does: Moves loose snow away from the unit so it can breathe and defrost water can drain. Caution: Snow and ice around the unit are slippery, and the fins bend easily.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.104`
5. Source caption: `From Daikin 3P515859-5S (p. 6), Bosch BOVA20 IOM (§2.3), and NEEP’s cold-climate install guide, checked October 11, 2026.`
6. Steps: “1. Only go out if you can stand on cleared, level ground in daylight. Don’t use a ladder or climb a snowbank. 2. Write down how the thermostat is set, then turn the system Off at the thermostat. 3. Clear loose snow from the ground around the unit and in front of the fan, by hand or with a soft broom, so air can move and defrost water can drain. Don’t clear snow off the coil or fins, and don’t touch them at all, by hand or with any tool. They bend easily. 4. Don’t use a shovel or snowblower near the unit, and don’t pile snow against it. 5. Leave ice alone: don’t chip, pry, or hit it, and don’t use hot water, a heat gun, or a torch. 6. Put the thermostat back the way you wrote it down.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.105`
7. Watch: “After you set the thermostat back, watch from inside for up to 15 minutes. A cloud of steam and a stopped outdoor fan can be part of a normal defrost.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.109`
8. Stop: “Stop if snow or ice is packed against the electrical box or disconnect, if there’s ice inside the grille, or if the footing is icy, and call a licensed HVAC professional. If ice is building up on the coil or the unit is encased in ice, leave the system Off at the thermostat, don’t chip the ice, and call a licensed HVAC professional.” `PENDING LEGAL sd.legal.106`
9. Undo: pn-v1 §3 undo line (REUSED; this page only. **Never rendered after an ice stop**: `ice_on_coil` routes to an ice-stop result, and results carry no undo line)

copy: Get everyone warm first. If someone is confused, very drowsy, or hard to wake, call 911. Then call a licensed HVAC professional and tell them the house is cold.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
If your thermostat has an Emergency Heat setting, switch to it to keep heat on without the outdoor unit while you wait for a pro. It usually costs more to run.

Stop. Running an iced-up outdoor unit can damage it. If your thermostat doesn’t have an Emergency Heat setting, turn the system Off at the thermostat. Let the ice melt on its own. Don’t chip ice, pour hot water on it, or try to speed up the defrost. If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first.
